name: Banded Ankle Mobilization
summary: A half-kneeling mobility drill using a resistance band anchored behind the ankle to promote posterior talar glide and improve dorsiflexion range of motion.

setup: Anchor a strong resistance band to a sturdy low point behind you, such as the bottom of a rack.
Step inside the loop and position the band across the front of the ankle, sitting just below the ankle bones (malleoli) over the talus.
Adopt a half-kneeling position with the banded foot forward, moving far enough out to create backward and downward tension from the band.
steps: Ensure the front heel is planted firmly and remains glued to the ground.
Drive your front knee directly forward over your middle toes into end-range dorsiflexion.
Hold the forward position briefly to feel the mobilization at the ankle joint.
Return the knee to the vertical starting position under control.
instructions.breathing: Inhale to prepare and exhale smoothly as you push your knee forward into dorsiflexion.
cues: Band stays below the ankle bones.
Track your knee over your second and third toes.

common_faults.fault: Placing the band too high on the lower shin.
common_faults.correction: Position the band directly over the talus below the malleoli so it mobilizes the joint instead of pulling the shin.

common_faults.fault: Heel lifting off the floor during the forward drive.
common_faults.correction: Only push the knee as far forward as allows the heel to remain completely flat on the ground.
Track the knee in line with or slightly outside the middle toes.

precautions: Verify that the band is attached to an immovable anchor before placing tension on it.
